states.name: Alabama
states.need: Private land, or a titled motorcycle with Class M. The §32-5A-267 e-bike exemption does not attach.
states.helmet: DOT helmet, all ages, if treated as a motorcycle. Class 3 e-bike 16+ does not apply.
states.notes: Pedals + under 750 W + class caps required for e-bike status. Untitled retail sale is normal; untitled road use is not.
states.ohv: Private property, or designated motorized OHV areas under land-manager rules.
states.takeaway: Alabama’s e-bike exemption is only for pedals + under 750 W + class speed caps, so a HAVØK is a motorcycle. Untitled retail sale is normal; untitled public-road riding is not.

states.name: Alaska
states.need: Highway use needs Alaska registration and M1/M2. Off-road follows DNR / USFS / BLM rules. Anchorage’s local e-bike ordinance still requires pedals and ≤750 W.
states.helmet: Motorcycle helmet under 18. Anchorage bicycle helmet under 16. Use a DOT helmet.
states.notes: No statewide e-bike statute (HB 8 vetoed 2023). A public-road ride is a motor-vehicle case.
states.ohv: Private land or designated motorized routes. Anchorage multiuse trails do not include this class.
states.takeaway: Alaska never adopted a statewide e-bike statute, so a HAVØK is a motorcycle if you put it on a public road. In Anchorage it is also outside AO 2024-51; ride private land or designated motorized routes.

states.name: Arizona
states.need: Arizona OHV decal on public motorized land, or a titled motorcycle with endorsement. Private land with permission.
states.helmet: Motorcycle helmet under 18. No statewide e-bike helmet. Standard MVD motorcycle age (typically 16+).
states.notes: ARS 28-101: pedals + <750 W. Canal paths and city multiuse paths are not a loophole.
states.ohv: Designated USFS/BLM motorized routes with OHV decal, or private land.
states.takeaway: Arizona e-bike status needs pedals and under 750 W; a HAVØK is a motorcycle or OHV. Ride designated motorized routes with an OHV decal, or private land — not canals, multiuse paths, or city streets as an 'e-bike.'
states.seller: A factory Class 1–3 / wattage label would be false under ARS 28-819(C).

states.name: Arkansas
states.need: Private land or motorized OHV areas. Street use only as a titled motorcycle / motor-driven cycle.
states.helmet: Motorcycle helmet generally under 21. No general Class 1/2 e-bike age that legalizes this machine.
states.notes: Electric Bicycle Act (pedals + <750 W). Rawrr already refuses vehicle shipments to Arkansas — peer precedent, not a HAVØK decision.
states.ohv: Private land or motorized OHV areas. State Parks Class 1 eMTB policy does not cover this class.
states.takeaway: Arkansas wrote a clean three-class e-bike act with a hard under-750 W line and required pedals, and a HAVØK is on the motorcycle side of that line. Untitled buy is fine; public-road riding is not an e-bike ride.

states.name: California
states.need: Green Sticker OHV ID for public OHV land, or private property under landowner control. No street plate for a stock off-highway eMoto. CHP / State Parks: originally off-highway units cannot convert to on-highway registration.
states.helmet: DOT FMVSS 218 helmet, all ages, as motorcycle/OHV. Highway M1 typically 16+ (permit from 15½). Youth OHV rules on public land.
states.notes: CVC 436.1 eMoto (SB 586). Cite-and-tow under CVC 22651.08 (AB 875). SB 1271 makes it a crime for a seller to advertise or label this as an e-bike — a California seller duty.
states.ohv: Designated OHV areas (SVRAs, BLM/USFS motorized routes) with Green Sticker, or private property. Not streets, sidewalks, bike lanes, or bike paths.
states.takeaway: A HAVØK O3/X1 is an eMoto in California, not an e-bike: get a Green Sticker and ride designated OHV land or private property only. Street, sidewalk, and bike-path riding is a cite-and-tow offense; aftermarket pedals do not change that.
states.seller: SB 1271 (2024): crime to advertise, sell, or label a non-qualifying vehicle as an electric bicycle. SB 1271 battery-safety labeling (UL 2272 / related) applies to powered mobility devices sold from 2026-01-01. A factory Class/wattage e-bike label is false labeling under CVC 312.5(d). SB 1167 (labeling / seller bans) was still moving in the Assembly as of 2026-08-20 — not law as of 2026-08-26.

states.name: Colorado
states.need: CPW OHV registration (resident card + decals) or nonresident/street-legal OHV permit for public land. Street use only as a titled motorcycle.
states.helmet: Motorcycle helmet under 18. Practical rule if stopped as a motorcycle: DOT helmet, all ages. CSP flagged under-16 e-moto operators in 2026.
states.notes: CSP statewide warning 2026-07-15: over 750 W, over 28 mph, or no functional pedals may be reclassified as a moped or motorcycle.
states.ohv: CPW-registered OHV on designated routes, or private land. Front Range paths are a stop.
states.takeaway: Colorado will not call an 8–21 kW 80 mph dirt bike an e-bike — CSP said so in July 2026. Register it with CPW as an OHV for designated routes, or keep it private; Front Range paths and streets are a stop.
states.seller: CSP 2026 warning targeted retailers selling high-speed electric motorcycles as bikes. A HAVØK cannot honestly wear a Class/wattage e-bike label (HB25-1197).

states.name: Connecticut
states.need: Private land, or DMV motor-driven-cycle / motorcycle registration if the unit is actually highway-capable. Dirt bikes are written out of the e-bike definition.
states.helmet: All-age helmet rule is for real e-bikes, not a hall pass here. Under-21 helmet for motor-driven cycles; motorcycle helmet if a motorcycle.
states.notes: C.G.S. §14-1(31) expressly excludes dirt bikes. 8–21 kW exceeds the 3,700 W motor-driven-cycle line used in CT DOT materials.
states.ohv: Private land. No Air Line / Farmington Canal / sidewalk / bike-path right.
states.takeaway: Connecticut wrote dirt bikes out of the e-bike definition on purpose. Pedals + under 750 W or you are a motor-driven cycle/motorcycle. A 15–21 kW HAVØK is not an e-bike even with clip-on pedals. All-age helmet rule is for real e-bikes, not a hall pass for emotos. Do not use public roads, sidewalks, or the Air Line/Farmington Canal paths on one of these machines.
states.seller: Public Act 25-159 (effective 2025-10-01): sellers must disclose in writing that out-of-class machines are motor vehicles and may be uninsured.

states.name: Delaware
states.need: Private land, or a titled motorcycle. Qualifying e-bike exemptions in §4198P do not attach.
states.helmet: Under 18 on any bicycle; all-ages helmet on Class 3 e-bikes — neither legalizes this class. DOT motorcycle helmet if a motorcycle.
states.notes: Pedals + seat + ≤750 W. Motor-on-sidewalk is banned even for legal Class 2.
states.ohv: Private land. Junction & Breakwater and sidewalks are off-limits.
states.takeaway: Delaware e-bikes need pedals, a seat, and ≤750 W. A HAVØK-class machine is a motorcycle or an illegal off-road bike. Do not use roads, the Junction & Breakwater Trail, or sidewalks (motor-on-sidewalk is banned even for legal Class 2).

states.name: District of Columbia
states.need: Private property only. DMV will not register a dirt bike. Loading onto a trailer to leave the District or reach private property is the narrow public-space exception.
states.helmet: Under-16 bicycle helmet. DOT helmet if treated as a motorcycle. Dirt-bike public operation is illegal at any age.
states.notes: D.C. Code §50-2201.04b: operating, parking, standing, or stopping a dirt bike on any public property is a crime; the vehicle is subject to forfeiture.
states.ohv: Private property only. No streets, sidewalks, or DDOT trails.
states.takeaway: In DC a Sur-Ron/Talaria/HAVØK-class machine is a dirt bike. Riding or even parking it on a public street is a crime, the DMV will not plate it, and the bike can be forfeited. Pedals plus a hard 20 mph motor cap are required for the unlicensed motorized-bicycle class — these bikes have neither.

states.name: Florida
states.need: Private land or purpose-built OHV/MX facilities. Street use only as a titled motorcycle with a motorcycle endorsement — many tax collectors refuse off-road-only MCO/VIN records. Unregistered road use is a criminal violation of F.S. §320.02(1).
states.helmet: Motorcycle: under 21 must wear FMVSS 218; 21+ may go without only with $10,000 medical-benefits coverage; eye protection required. Do not put a minor on a 60 mph machine on a public street.
states.notes: Not an e-bike and not a moped (moped ≤2 bhp / ≤30 mph). Untitled purchase is easy; untitled street riding is a criminal registration case.
states.ohv: Private property or purpose-built OHV/MX. No statewide OHV plate that legalizes street use. Not sidewalks, bike lanes, beaches, or dunes.
states.takeaway: Florida draws three boxes — e-bike (<750W, pedals, 20/28 mph), moped (pedals, ≤2 bhp, ≤30 mph), and motorcycle — and a HAVØK is the third box, usually not even titleable at the tax collector. Untitled purchase is easy; untitled street riding is a criminal registration case.

states.name: Georgia
states.need: Private land, or a registered motorcycle with Class M, insurance, and motorcycle equipment.
states.helmet: DOT helmet, all ages, plus eye protection if a motorcycle. Class III e-bike 15+ does not apply.
states.notes: DPS-34 (July 2024) is the official 750 W electric-assisted-bicycle line. Older 1,000 W web pages are stale.
states.ohv: Private land or motorized OHV areas. No bike lanes, cycle tracks, or shared-use paths.
states.takeaway: Georgia requires pedals and ≤750 W for e-bike treatment; a HAVØK is a motorcycle problem, not an e-bike. Untitled purchase is fine; public-road riding without Class M, plate, and insurance is not.

states.name: Hawaii
states.need: Private property is the clean path. Street use would require motorcycle registration and insurance, which a stock off-road unit generally cannot obtain. The $30 county e-bike decal is not available in good faith.
states.helmet: Motorcycle helmet, all ages. Act 259 raised e-bike helmets to under 18 — that is for real e-bikes.
states.notes: Act 259 (signed 2026-07-15): a two- or three-wheeler capable of exceeding 28 mph on electric power is an electric motorcycle. HPD: non-qualifying high-power devices stay off public roads, bike lanes, sidewalks, and shared-use paths.
states.ohv: Private property. County and NPS park rules remain restrictive.
states.takeaway: Since July 15, 2026, Hawaii calls anything that can do over 28 mph on electric power an electric motorcycle and keeps it off roads, lanes, sidewalks, and paths unless it is a real registered motorcycle. A HAVØK is private-property or (if you can actually title it) a motorcycle — not a $30 e-bike.
states.seller: Act 259: manufacturers must label class, top assisted speed, and wattage and give buyers a state-law pamphlet (sales rules phased 120 days after signing). A HAVØK cannot be labeled as a Class 1/2/3 e-bike.

states.name: Idaho
states.need: Idaho OHV sticker on public motorized routes, or private land. Street use only as a titled motorcycle/moped.
states.helmet: Motorcycle helmet under 18. OHV youth helmet rules on public land. Class 3 e-bike 15+ does not apply.
states.notes: I.C. 49-106: pedals + <750 W. HB 500 (2026) is about true e-bike collision language, not a legalization of this class.
states.ohv: OHV sticker on motorized routes, or private land. Boise Greenbelt and Trail of the Coeur d'Alenes are not a loophole.
states.takeaway: Idaho’s <750 W / pedal class system does not cover a HAVØK. Use an OHV sticker on motorized routes or keep it on private land; Greenbelt and city paths are not a loophole.
states.seller: A class/speed/wattage e-bike label cannot honestly be applied.

states.name: Illinois
states.roads: Not as an e-bike (statutory gap over 28 mph)
states.need: Private land unless you can actually title, plate, insure, and equip it as a motorcycle or motor-driven cycle. Recheck SB 3484 after 2026-08-29; any new MDC rules would start 2027-01-01.
states.helmet: No statewide motorcycle or e-bike helmet mandate. Eye protection required if treated as a motorcycle / MDC / moped (625 ILCS 5/11-1404). Practical motorcycle age generally 16+.
states.notes: Current law does not clearly govern devices over 28 mph. Enrolled SB 3484 (to Governor 2026-06-30; 60-day deadline 2026-08-29) would, if enacted, treat 750 W–8 kW electric devices as motor-driven cycles on 2027-01-01. O3 sits on that 8 kW ceiling; O3 Pro and X1 sit above it as ordinary motorcycles.
states.ohv: Private land. No sidewalk, bike-lane, or bike-path right. Chicago-area departments already ticket or impound dirt-bike-style electric two-wheelers.
states.takeaway: Do not ride a HAVØK O3/O3 Pro/X1 on Illinois streets, bike lanes, or paths as an e-bike. Pedals are required for e-bike status and these bikes are 10–28× the watt cap. Keep it on private land unless you can actually title, plate, insure, and equip it as a motorcycle/MDC. Recheck SB 3484 after 2026-08-29; any new motor-driven-cycle rules start 2027-01-01.
states.seller: Sale as an e-bike is not a defense. SB 3484, if enacted, would add VIN/speedometer/FMVSS-style rules for new motor-driven cycles.

states.name: Indiana
states.need: BMV ORV title (purchases after 2009-12-31) and ORV registration for dirt. An ORV may not be operated on a highway. Street use only as a fully street-legal motorcycle.
states.helmet: Motorcycle helmet under 18. Motorcycle generally 16+. Youth ORV supervision rules apply.
states.notes: True electric bicycles are excluded from the ORV definition — these machines do not get that carve-out. BMV will not issue a highway plate to an ORV just because lights were added.
states.ohv: DNR ORV areas (Interlake, Redbird) with ORV registration plus a trail-use permit. Private land otherwise.
states.takeaway: Not an e-bike in Indiana. Title/register it as an ORV for dirt. Do not put it on public roads unless it is a fully street-legal motorcycle. Pedals would still not save an 8 kW, 60 mph machine.

states.name: Iowa
states.need: Iowa DOT motorcycle title for highways. Public dirt: DNR off-road motorcycle/ATV registration under chapter 321I.
states.helmet: Motorcycle helmet under 18. Motorcycle generally 16+.
states.notes: Iowa Code 321.1(36A): pedals + less than 750 W. Motorized bicycle is capped at 39 mph — a 60+ mph machine is a motorcycle.
states.ohv: Designated ATV/OHM riding areas with DNR registration, or private land.
states.takeaway: Not an Iowa e-bike. Pedals and <750 W are mandatory. Public roads only as a registered motorcycle. Public dirt only with DNR off-road motorcycle/ATV registration. Private land otherwise.

states.name: Kansas
states.need: Motorcycle title, plate, endorsement, and liability insurance for any public road, or keep it on private land.
states.helmet: Motorcycle helmet under 18. Motorcycle generally 16+.
states.notes: K.S.A. 8-1489: less than 750 W + pedals. Kansas ATV definition is 3+ tires — not an automatic sticker path for a two-wheel machine.
states.ohv: Private land. State-park e-bike policies do not create access for a 60 mph dirt-style machine.
states.takeaway: Not a Kansas e-bike. Title and insure it as a motorcycle for any public road, or keep it on private land. Pedals would not save 8–21 kW / 60+ mph.

states.name: Kentucky
states.roads: Gray as statute, illegal as power/speed
states.need: Private land, or motorcycle / electric-motorcycle title, plate, insurance, and license. There is no Kentucky e-bike box to hide in. Exceeds the moped box (≤2 bhp / ≤30 mph).
states.helmet: Motorcycle helmet rules apply if classified as a motorcycle. No statewide e-bike age.
states.notes: Weakest statewide statute in the South — that helps the rider less, not more. KRS 186.010 added electric motorcycle as of 2026-07-15. Louisville warned after a 2025–26 unregistered electric-motorcycle crash.
states.ohv: Private land. Louisville Metro / The Parklands distinguish bicycles from electric motorcycles. Fort Mitchell–style local class ordinances were spreading in Kenton County in August 2026.
states.takeaway: Kentucky has no Class 1/2/3 e-bike law to hide in, and a HAVØK is faster and stronger than a moped, so highway use is a motorcycle/electric-motorcycle problem. Untitled purchase is easy; untitled street riding is what Louisville just warned about.

states.name: Louisiana
states.need: Private land, or a registered motorcycle with a motorcycle license.
states.helmet: Louisiana all-ages motorcycle helmet on public roads. Do not read the Class 3 age-12 rule onto a 60 mph machine.
states.notes: La. R.S. 32:1: pedals + <750 W + Class 1/2/3. Untitled purchase is normal.
states.ohv: Private land. No sidewalks or non-motorized trails.
states.takeaway: Louisiana’s e-bike class system still requires pedals and under 750 W, so a HAVØK is a motorcycle. Untitled purchase is normal; public-road use needs a plate and a motorcycle license.

states.name: Maine
states.need: Private land. Qualifying e-bike exemptions (no license / plate / insurance) stop at <750 W with real pedals.
states.helmet: Under 16 bicycle helmet on a real e-bike. Motorcycle helmet if reclassified. Class 2/3 e-bike operator 16+ does not apply.
states.notes: Tampering that lets the motor assist above class speed means the vehicle is no longer an electric bicycle (29-A M.R.S. §2063(14)(C)).
states.ohv: Private land. Stay off carriage roads, Acadia (federal 750 W / pedal rules), and bike paths.
states.takeaway: Maine's e-bike free pass (no license, plate, or insurance) stops at <750 W with real pedals. A HAVØK-class 60 mph dirt bike is a motorcycle. Stay off public roads, carriage roads, and bike paths.

states.name: Maryland
states.need: Private land. Dirt bikes / minibikes are generally not Title-13 registerable. Over-limit devices that can meet FMVSS follow moped/motorcycle paper.
states.helmet: Under 16 bicycle helmet on a real e-bike. DOT helmet and eye protection if moped/motorcycle. Class 3 e-bike 16+ does not apply.
states.notes: Md. Transportation Code §11-117.1: pedals + ≤750 W. Most state parks allow only Class 1 e-bikes.
states.ohv: Private land. Not Capital Crescent (Class 1 only on the MD side) or state-park trails.
states.takeaway: Maryland e-bike status requires pedals and ≤750 W. A HAVØK-class dirt bike is a dirt bike or an unregistered motorcycle, not a bicycle. Do not ride it on public roads, the Capital Crescent (Class 1 only on the MD side), or state-park trails.

states.name: Massachusetts
states.need: Private land. Massachusetts has Class 1–2 only (no Class 3). A 60+ mph machine exceeds the 25 mph moped cap and needs a motorcycle path it usually cannot complete.
states.helmet: DOT FMVSS 218 helmet if treated as a motorized bicycle or motorcycle. Motorized bicycle: 16+ with license/permit.
states.notes: Governor Healey’s Ride Safe Act was in conference as of 2026-08-03 and is not law. E-bikes are banned from all sidewalks statewide.
states.ohv: Private land. No DCR paths, sidewalks, or public ways as sold.
states.takeaway: Massachusetts has no Class 3 and no 750 W exception. A HAVØK-class throttle dirt bike is not an e-bike even if the box says it is. Pedals are required. The only theoretical on-road path is RMV motorcycle (or, if somehow ≤25 mph, moped) registration — which these 60+ mph off-road-form bikes almost never qualify for. Stay off public ways, sidewalks, and DCR paths.

states.name: Michigan
states.need: Public dirt: annual DNR ORV license plus trail permit on designated trails. Public roads: SOS assembled-vehicle title, plate, no-fault, and a motorcycle endorsement.
states.helmet: ORV: crash helmet and protective eyewear on public land. Motorcycle endorsement generally 16+. Class 3 e-bike 14+ does not apply.
states.notes: DNR e-moto test: over 750 W, over 28 mph under motor assist, primarily throttle-powered above 20 mph, or no fully operable pedals.
states.ohv: Designated ORV routes/trails with license + trail permit, or private land. E-motos are strictly prohibited on nonmotorized trails.
states.takeaway: Michigan will not call a HAVØK an e-bike. Pedals and ≤750 W are mandatory. Public roads only as a titled, plated, insured motorcycle. Public dirt only with a DNR ORV license (and trail permit on designated trails). Private land is the cleanest use. Do not use bike paths.

states.name: Minnesota
states.need: DNR OHM registration is required for operation in Minnesota, including exclusive private-property use. Public roads need a second, street-legal motorcycle registration (dual registration).
states.helmet: Under 18 must wear an approved helmet on public land, frozen waters, and road rights-of-way. Motorcycle generally 16+.
states.notes: Unusually strict anti-unlock statute: a product sold to run 60+ mph cannot be an e-bike even with dummy pedals. The 2026 POS e-moto registration bill failed.
states.ohv: Private land still needs the DNR OHM registration (decal display waived on private property; the registration is not). State trails and park-district trails are off-limits.
states.takeaway: Minnesota will not treat a HAVØK as an e-bike. Register it with DNR as an off-highway motorcycle even if you only ride private land. Public roads require a second, street-legal motorcycle registration. Bike paths and state trails are off-limits.

states.name: Mississippi
states.need: Private land, or a titled motorcycle with license, insurance, and an all-ages helmet.
states.helmet: All-ages approved motorcycle helmet (Miss. Code §63-7-64) if used as a motorcycle on a road. Class 3 e-bike 16+ does not apply.
states.notes: HB 1195 (2021) is still the framework: pedals + <750 W. The dirt-bike exemption in §63-3-1315 is for qualifying e-bikes, not a 21 kW machine.
states.ohv: Private land. Stay off sidewalks, Natchez Trace non-motorized use, and mountain-bike trails.
states.takeaway: Mississippi’s e-bike law is pedals + under 750 W + class caps; a HAVØK is a motorcycle. Untitled buy is fine; a public-road ride without a plate and helmet is not.

states.name: Missouri
states.need: Private land, or a titled, insured motorcycle with a motorcycle-qualified license.
states.helmet: Motorcycle helmet under 18 (RSMo 302.020). Class 3 e-bike 16+ does not apply.
states.notes: RSMo 307.194 exemptions (no title/registration/license/insurance) apply only to electric bicycles.
states.ohv: Private land. Katy Trail / state-park e-bike policies do not create access. No bike-path privilege.
states.takeaway: Missouri will not treat a HAVØK as an e-bike. Pedals and <750 W are mandatory. No bike-path privilege. Public roads only as a titled, insured motorcycle. Otherwise private land.

states.name: Montana
states.need: Private land or designated motorized routes with the land-manager OHV permit. Street use only as a titled motorcycle.
states.helmet: No statewide bicycle or adult motorcycle helmet. Billings has an under-16 bicycle ordinance. Use a DOT helmet.
states.notes: No three-class system (SB 387 died 2025). Only test: motor cannot push a 170-lb rider past 20 mph on the flat.
states.ohv: Designated motorized routes or private land. DNRC treats even qualifying e-bikes as motorized on state trust land.
states.takeaway: Montana’s only e-bike test is 20 mph with a 170-lb rider — a HAVØK fails it. Ride designated motorized routes or private land; do not count on bicycle rules.

states.name: Nebraska
states.need: Private land, or a registered, titled, insured motorcycle with a motorcycle endorsement and a helmet.
states.helmet: Universal motorcycle helmet state — operators and passengers if the device is a motorcycle. Motorcycle generally 16+.
states.notes: Pedals + 750 W + 1 brake horsepower. ATV/minibike non-registration is not a street loophole (ATV is 3+ tires).
states.ohv: Private land. Do not use bike paths.
states.takeaway: Not a Nebraska e-bike (pedals + 750 W + 1 bhp required). On public roads it is a motorcycle: license, title, plate, insurance, helmet. Otherwise private land. Do not use bike paths.

states.name: Nevada
states.need: Nevada OHV title/registration decal on public OHV land (short-term nonresident exception may apply). Street use only as a titled motorcycle.
states.helmet: Motorcycle helmet under 18; 18+ optional for street motorcycles. Clark County / Henderson add minor-helmet and park rules.
states.notes: NRS 484B.017: pedals + ≤750 W + class speeds. The Strip and Henderson will not treat this as a bicycle.
states.ohv: Public OHV land with NV OHV decal, or private land. BLM Red Rock: motorized roads only.
states.takeaway: Nevada’s e-bike law is pedal + 750 W + 20/28 mph — a HAVØK is a motorcycle or OHV. Register it for OHV land or keep it private; the Strip and Henderson will not treat it as a bicycle.

states.name: New Hampshire
states.need: Places OHRVs are allowed, or private land. Street use only as a registered motorcycle.
states.helmet: Class 3 under-18 helmet is for real e-bikes. Motorcycle/OHRV helmet rules if so classified.
states.notes: Must be a pedaled vehicle with a motor of less than 750 W. Exactly 750 W fails.
states.ohv: OHRV-legal areas or private land. Not roads, rail trails, or town bike paths.
states.takeaway: New Hampshire e-bike law is a pedaled-vehicle statute. A throttle dirt bike with an 8–21 kW motor is an OHRV/motorcycle, not a bicycle. Do not ride it on public roads, rail trails, or town bike paths.

states.name: New Jersey
states.need: Lawful off-road / ORV areas only as a dirt bike. Street use only as a motorcycle with plates, a motorcycle license, and insurance. Dirt bikes cannot be street-registered and may only cross a highway under 39:3C-17.
states.helmet: USDOT helmet for motorized-bicycle and motorcycle classes. Dirt-bike / ORV operators generally 18+ where off-road use is lawful (39:3C-16). Real e-bike / motorized-bicycle floor is 15+ — that floor does not legalize this machine.
states.notes: After July 19, 2026 every real e-bike needs MVC registration and a license. 8–21 kW / 60+ mph is a motorcycle (if it has real pedals) or an impoundable dirt bike (if it does not). Ridgewood and other PDs are impounding this exact class under 39:3C-35 (first-offense reclaim fee $500).
states.ohv: Lawful ORV areas or private land. Not streets, sidewalks, parks, or bike paths.
states.takeaway: New Jersey is the hardest 'buy as an e-bike, ride tomorrow' state in this set. After July 19, 2026 every real e-bike needs MVC registration and a license; anything 8–21 kW / 60+ mph is a motorcycle or an illegal dirt bike. Pedals are required even for the motorcycle-adjacent 'electric motorized bicycle' definition. Riding a HAVØK-class machine on a public street without motorcycle plates, a motorcycle license, and insurance is an impoundable offense.
states.seller: Sellers of real low-speed e-bikes / motorized bicycles must hand out Form BA-49EB. These machines are out of that class. Do not register or label them as e-bikes.

states.name: New Mexico
states.need: New Mexico OHV permit on public OHV land, or a titled motorcycle with endorsement.
states.helmet: Motorcycle helmet, all operators and passengers. Child Helmet Safety Act under 18 is for bicycles / qualifying e-bikes.
states.notes: NMSA 66-1-4.5: pedals + ≤750 W. Albuquerque adopted the state classes — this class gets none of that access.
states.ohv: Motorized routes with the right permit, or private land. Not the Bosque or city multiuse paths.
states.takeaway: New Mexico e-bike path rights stop at 750 W and pedals. A HAVØK is an OHV/motorcycle — use motorized routes with the right permit, not the Bosque or city multiuse paths.

states.name: New York
states.need: Private land only as sold. NY DMV: dirt bikes / off-road motorcycles may not be operated on public streets, sidewalks, or parking lots and generally cannot be street-registered. A FMVSS-certified limited-use motorcycle or motorcycle with a plate and motorcycle license is the only on-road path — typical dirt-bike form cannot get that plate.
states.helmet: 16+ to operate any real e-bike (does not apply). Motorcycle helmet if classified as a motorcycle. AG recommends helmets for all.
states.notes: NY AG consumer alert July 31, 2026: marketing or selling over-limit devices as e-bikes is unlawful. NYC DOT caps e-device operation at 15 mph citywide (effective 2025-10-24) and NYPD has been seizing illegal e-motos. Expect ticket, seizure, and in NYC possible forfeiture.
states.ohv: Private land. ATV registration is for designated off-road use only and is not a street plate. Not streets, sidewalks, bike lanes, or parks.
states.takeaway: Do not ride a HAVØK O3/O3 Pro/X1 (or any Sur-Ron/Talaria-class 60+ mph throttle dirt bike) on NYC or NYS public streets, bike lanes, or sidewalks as an 'e-bike.' Pedals are required and even with pedals these motors are 10–28× the 750 W cap. Retail 'no registration' is a sales practice, not a legal status. Expect ticket, seizure, and (in NYC) possible criminal/forfeiture exposure. Only a FMVSS-certified, plated motorcycle/LUM with a motorcycle license is a lawful on-road path — and typical dirt-bike-form emotos cannot get that plate.
states.seller: NY AG (2026-07-31): selling or marketing over-limit devices as e-bikes is illegal. Report line 800-771-7755. Do not call O3 / O3 Pro / X1 an e-bike in New York advertising, cart copy, or shipping inserts.

states.name: North Carolina
states.need: Private land, or a registered motorcycle if the unit is titleable. UNC SOG walks over-~30 mph straight into motorcycle: license, registration, insurance.
states.helmet: NC motorcycle helmet on public roads if classified as a motorcycle. Typically 16+ for motorcycle licensing.
states.notes: Current single class: pedals + ≤750 W + ≤20 mph motor-only. SL 2026-46 (effective 2026-12-01) adds Class 3 but still caps 750 W — it does not legalize this class.
states.ohv: Private land. SL 2026-46 lets locals regulate true e-bikes on paths starting Dec 1, 2026 — still not an invitation for 21 kW.
states.takeaway: North Carolina’s e-bike box is pedals + ≤750 W + ≤20 mph motor-only until Dec 1, 2026, then a still-capped three-class box — a HAVØK never fits. Untitled purchase is normal; untitled highway use is a motorcycle case.

states.name: North Dakota
states.need: Private land, or a titled, plated, insured motorcycle with the proper license. The e-bike title exemption is e-bike-only.
states.helmet: Motorcycle helmet under 18. Motorcycle generally 16+.
states.notes: NDCC 39-01-01(19): pedals + 750 W or fewer. A two-wheel electric dirt bike used off-highway may also be an OHV under chapter 39-29 — it is still not an e-bike.
states.ohv: Private land, or OHV rules if the land unit requires them. Not sidewalks, paths, or non-motorized trails.
states.takeaway: Not a North Dakota e-bike. Register and insure it as a motorcycle for any public road, or keep it off public roads. Pedals are required for e-bike status and these bikes do not have a legal motor.

states.name: Ohio
states.need: Private land you own or control (OHM sticker not required if used exclusively there). Public off-road land: Ohio OHM registration (title required first). Streets: full motorcycle conversion, Highway Patrol inspection, BMV plate, endorsement, insurance.
states.helmet: Motorcycle helmet under 18. Eye protection required. Street-legal motorcycle generally 16+ with endorsement.
states.notes: Municipal pages (Beavercreek, Mason) already say e-moto / electric dirt bikes without operable pedals may not use roadways, sidewalks, or shared-use paths unless fully street-legal.
states.ohv: Land you own/control, or designated off-road areas with OHM/APV registration.
states.takeaway: Ohio will not treat a HAVØK as an e-bike. Pedals and <750 W are mandatory. Unregistered 60+ mph bikes cannot use public roads. Options: private land (OHM sticker not required if exclusively on land you own/control) or Ohio OHM registration for public off-road land, or a full motorcycle conversion for streets.

states.name: Oklahoma
states.need: Private land, or a registered motorcycle with a motorcycle endorsement.
states.helmet: Motorcycle helmet generally under 18. Class 3 e-bike 16+ does not apply.
states.notes: Requires pedals, ≤750 W, CPSC bicycle construction, and a motor that dies when you stop pedaling — the opposite of this machine. Rawrr already refuses vehicle shipments to Oklahoma.
states.ohv: Private land. Oklahoma OHV / public-land motorized rules do not convert the machine into an e-bike.
states.takeaway: Oklahoma’s e-bike statute requires pedals, ≤750 W, CPSC bicycle construction, and a motor that dies when you stop pedaling — the opposite of a HAVØK dirt-bike e-moto. Untitled purchase is normal; street use is a motorcycle problem.

states.name: Oregon
states.need: Oregon ATV operating permit (Class III motorcycle) on public OHV land, or private property. Highway motorcycle/moped title is usually unavailable on stock off-road units.
states.helmet: Motorcycle helmet, all ages, if operated as motorcycle/moped. ATV helmet rules on public OHV land, especially for youth. 16+ for a real electric assisted bicycle — N/A here.
states.notes: ORS 801.258 Class 1/2/3 (HB 4103). Moped is capped at 30 mph unassisted — these machines exceed that too. Reported 2026 HB 4007 on 'imposter' e-bike sales — confirm before citing as enacted.
states.ohv: Permitted OHV land or private property. Not pavement as an e-bike. Not sidewalks or shared paths.
states.takeaway: Oregon’s e-bike class (and any leftover 1,000 W lore) does not cover an 8–21 kW 80 mph throttle dirt bike. Ride it as a Class III ATV on permitted OHV land, or keep it on private property; pavement as an 'e-bike' is not legal.

states.name: Pennsylvania
states.need: Private land. Pennsylvania’s bicycle box also requires ≤100 lb, ≤750 W, ≤20 mph motor-only, and pedals — these machines fail all four. PennDOT typically cannot title units that lack a 17-digit VIN and FMVSS motorcycle equipment.
states.helmet: 16+ to operate a real pedalcycle with electric assist. DOT motorcycle helmet if classified as a motorcycle. No helmet for a real moped per PennDOT — these machines exceed the 25 mph moped cap anyway.
states.notes: No Class 1/2/3 system. Weight alone knocks out most Sur-Ron / Talaria-class frames.
states.ohv: Private land. Not roads, DCNR bike trails, sidewalks, or bike paths.
states.takeaway: Pennsylvania will never treat a 100+ lb, 8–21 kW, 60 mph throttle dirt bike as a bicycle. Pedals, 100 lb, 750 W, and 20 mph are all mandatory. You can buy it without a plate; you cannot lawfully ride it on a public road, trail, or sidewalk as an e-bike, and you probably cannot title it as a motorcycle either.

states.name: Rhode Island
states.need: Private land. The e-bike exemption is for ≤2 SAE hp and ≤28 mph. Residents must register motorcycles and non-exempt motorized bicycles.
states.helmet: Under 21 CPSC helmet on a real e-bike. Motorcycle helmet if classified as a motorcycle. 16+ to operate an electric motorized bicycle — N/A here.
states.notes: Two overlapping definitions (class system + 2 hp / 28 mph) both exclude 8–21 kW / 60 mph. H 7789 (2026) is a bill, not law.
states.ohv: Private land. Not the East Bay Bike Path.
states.takeaway: Rhode Island's e-bike exemption is for ≤2 SAE hp and ≤28 mph class-legal bikes, not 8–21 kW dirt bikes. Pedals and the 28 mph cap are the line. Buying unregistered is normal; riding on RI roads or the East Bay Bike Path as an 'e-bike' is not legal.

states.name: South Carolina
states.need: Private land. Also over the 1,500 W electric-moped cap, so motorcycle is the remaining statutory box — and stock units often cannot be plated.
states.helmet: Motorcycle helmet generally under 21 if classified as a motorcycle. No statewide e-bike age.
states.notes: S.C. Code §56-1-10(29) is the federal CPSC box: pedals, ≤750 W, under 20 mph motor-only. Locals (Hilton Head, Charleston, Grand Strand) add path and beach rules.
states.ohv: Private land. Not sidewalks, beach paths, or non-motorized trails.
states.takeaway: South Carolina’s e-bike law is the federal CPSC box (pedals, ≤750 W, under 20 mph motor-only), and a HAVØK is also over the 1,500 W electric-moped cap. Untitled purchase is easy; public-road use needs a motorcycle path most stock bikes cannot complete.
states.seller: Labeling as an e-bike is not a defense.

states.name: South Dakota
states.need: Private land, or title, plate, insurance, and equipment as a motorcycle / motor-driven cycle.
states.helmet: Motorcycle helmet under 18. Class III e-bike 16+ does not apply.
states.notes: Sioux Falls PD (2026, local guidance): motors over 750 W or assistance beyond 28 mph classify the vehicle as a moped; no pedals means it is not an e-bike.
states.ohv: Private land. Path rights in 32-20B are e-bike-only.
states.takeaway: South Dakota will not treat a HAVØK as an e-bike. Pedals and ≤750 W are mandatory. Public roads only if you can title, plate, insure, and equip it as a motorcycle/moped. Otherwise private land only.

states.name: Tennessee
states.need: Private land, or a registered motorcycle / motor-driven cycle with Class M and insurance.
states.helmet: All-ages motorcycle helmet on public roads. Class 3 e-bike 16+ (reported 2026 raise) does not apply.
states.notes: T.C.A. §55-8-301: pedals + <750 W + class caps. PC 823 exemptions do not follow a hangtag.
states.ohv: Private land. No sidewalks, greenways, or non-motorized singletrack.
states.takeaway: Tennessee’s e-bike statute is pedals + under 750 W + 20/28 mph class caps, so a HAVØK is a motorcycle. Buy untitled if you want; do not treat greenways or city streets as legal riding.

states.name: Texas
states.need: Private land, or a current TPWD OHV decal ($16, valid Sept 1–Aug 31) at a public OHV venue. Street use only as a titled, plated, insured motorcycle with Class M — most factory off-road units lack FMVSS certification and a registerable 17-digit VIN, so that path is gray-to-closed.
states.helmet: If treated as a motorcycle on a public street: under 21 must wear approved headgear; 21+ may ride without if they completed an approved motorcycle course or have qualifying medical coverage. TPWD OHV land requires safety apparel. No statewide minimum for private-property riding. Motorcycle on public roads: 16 with Class M path.
states.notes: Tex. Transp. Code §664.001 will never treat 8–21 kW / 60+ mph as an e-bike. Allen PD publishes tickets, parental citations, and impound for unregistered e-motorcycles. Rawrr already refuses vehicle shipments to Texas — peer precedent, not a HAVØK decision.
states.ohv: Private land with owner permission, or designated OHV parks/trails with a TPWD decal. Not streets, sidewalks, bike lanes, or non-motorized trails.
states.takeaway: Texas will never treat an 8–21 kW / 60+ mph HAVØK as an e-bike, pedals or not. Buy it untitled if you want, then ride private land or a TPWD OHV park with a $16 decal — public streets without a motorcycle title, plate, insurance, and Class M is the ticket/impound path.
states.seller: §502.143(4) only bars registering a true electric bicycle; it is not a loophole for 8 kW+ machines. Do not merchandise this class as an e-bike in Texas.

states.name: Utah
states.need: OHV registration sticker (or nonresident $30 permit) plus the Utah OHV Education Course (required under 18; adult course also required statewide since 2023). Street use needs motorcycle title, endorsement, and insurance.
states.helmet: Helmet required for operators under 18 on OHV/motorcycle; recommended all ages. Highway motorcycle: standard licensing.
states.notes: One of the strictest statutes: factory-affixed cranks are mandatory, and pedal kits / peg bikes are carved out. Vehicles advertised or designed to do 20+ mph on motor alone are excluded.
states.ohv: Motorized / OHV routes with sticker and education certificate, or private land. Moab Class 1 e-MTB access does not include this class.
states.takeaway: Utah wrote pedal-kit and 20 mph-on-throttle exclusions for exactly this product class. Register the HAVØK as an OHV, take the education course, and stay on motorized routes.
states.seller: Do not advertise a 20+ mph-on-throttle machine as an electric assisted bicycle — the statute excludes vehicles advertised that way.

states.name: Vermont
states.need: Private land. Qualifying e-bike exemptions (no license, plate, insurance, or helmet) are only for <750 W bikes with real pedals.
states.helmet: No statewide bicycle or e-bike helmet mandate. Motorcycle helmet if the device is a motorcycle. Class 3 e-bike 16+ does not apply.
states.notes: A separate 'motor-assisted bicycle' box (under 1,000 W, throttle not over 20 mph) also does not fit 8–21 kW / 60+ mph.
states.ohv: Private land. Not public highways, the Island Line, or town paths.
states.takeaway: Vermont's e-bike exemption is generous (no license, plate, insurance, or helmet) — but only for <750 W bikes with real pedals. A 60 mph 8–21 kW dirt bike is a motor vehicle. Do not ride it on public highways, the Island Line, or town paths as an e-bike.

states.name: Virginia
states.need: Private land. Street-legal only if titled as a motorcycle with Class M. James City County Police: electric dirt bikes without pedals, over 35 mph, are off-road motorcycles and may be impounded.
states.helmet: Virginia motorcycle helmet for operators and passengers if classified as a motorcycle. Motorcycle license typically 16+.
states.notes: Va. Code §46.2-100: pedals + ≤750 W input. Virginia’s moped box (≤1500 W and ≤35 mph) also does not fit.
states.ohv: Private land. Not public roads, sidewalks, or most trails.
states.takeaway: Virginia will not call a 60+ mph / 8 kW+ dirt-bike-shaped throttle machine an e-bike. Buy it untitled if you want and ride private land; public pavement without a motorcycle title and Class M is the impound conversation JCC PD already published.

states.name: Washington
states.need: ORV permit/tab under RCW 46.09 for public off-road land. Highway use would require motorcycle or moped registration — stock off-road units usually lack the equipment/VIN path.
states.helmet: DOT motorcycle helmet, operator and passenger, on highways if classified as motorcycle/moped/motor-driven cycle. Motorcycle typically 16+ with endorsement; extra $250 penalty for no endorsement.
states.notes: ESSB 6110 (effective 2026-06-11) expressly excludes any vehicle capable of exceeding 20 mph on the motor alone, and vehicles designed to be easily reconfigured out of class.
states.ohv: ORV-permitted public land or private land. Class 3 e-bikes are already barred from shared-use paths; this class is worse.
states.takeaway: From June 11, 2026, anything that can do more than 20 mph on the throttle is not an e-bike in Washington. Treat a HAVØK as an unregistrable motorcycle on pavement and as an ORV off-road.
states.seller: ESSB 6110 anti-defeat / easy-reconfigure exclusion matters if a seller claims a hidden 20 mph mode.

states.name: West Virginia
states.need: Private land, or a registered motorcycle with a license. Official §17C-11-8(c): exceed a §17C-1-70 limit and the vehicle is no longer an electric bicycle.
states.helmet: West Virginia motorcycle helmet on public roads if classified as a motorcycle. Under-15 helmet is a bicycle rule and does not legalize this class.
states.notes: Pedals + fewer than 750 W. The private-property anti-tamper carve-out is not a highway grant.
states.ohv: Private land. Class 1/2 path rights are for true e-bikes only.
states.takeaway: West Virginia’s e-bike law requires pedals and fewer than 750 W, so a HAVØK is a motorcycle the moment it leaves private property. Untitled purchase is fine; public-road riding needs a motorcycle title and license.

states.name: Wisconsin
states.need: DNR public-use OHM registration ($30 / 2-year) for designated OHM trails and signed OHM road routes. Highway use needs WisDOT motorcycle title, plate, insurance, and a motorcycle license — missing VIN is a practical bar.
states.helmet: Under-18 motorcycle helmet is the usual statewide rule if classified as motorcycle/OHM. Motorcycle generally 16+.
states.notes: WisDOT: over class speeds see moped; devices that can exceed about 30 mph are motorcycles. August 2026 local reporting: consumer products without a VIN cannot be registered and cannot legally be ridden on the road.
states.ohv: Private land (private-use OHM sticker is voluntary), or designated OHM facilities with a public-use sticker. Not bike lanes, separated paths, or sidewalks.
states.takeaway: Wisconsin will not treat a HAVØK as an e-bike. Unregistered 60+ mph use on public roads is not legal, and missing VIN may make street-legal conversion impossible. Private land, or DNR OHM public-use registration on designated OHM land, are the realistic options.

states.name: Wyoming
states.need: Wyoming ORV permit/sticker on public ORV land, or private land. Street use only as a titled motorcycle.
states.helmet: Motorcycle/ORV helmet under 18. Recommended all ages. Highway motorcycle: standard licensing.
states.notes: W.S. 31-5-707 exemptions attach only if the machine is an electric bicycle under 31-1-101 (pedals + <750 W).
states.ohv: Public motorized routes with ORV sticker, or private land. Jackson / Teton County are active on pathways.
states.takeaway: Wyoming e-bike exemptions in 31-5-707 do not attach to a 15 kW dirt bike. Get an ORV sticker for public motorized routes or keep it on private land.
states.seller: E-bike manufacturer label (class, top assisted speed, wattage) cannot honestly be applied.
